procnotices.notice_text:
ECOWAS REGIONAL ELECTRICITY ACCESS PROJECT (ECOWAS-REAP)

Project – P164044

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

RECRUITMENT OF AN INDEPENDENT EVALUATOR FOR END OF REAP PROJECT EVALUATION

                                       NG-ECOWAS-DEM-539424-CS-INDV

Closing Date: 21st, May 2026 at 5:00 pm GMT

Contract: Lump sum

  1.  Background and justification of the project

The energy sector in the ECOWAS region faces enduring challenges in achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly the objective 7, which aims to ensure universal access to affordable, reliable and modern energy services. Access to energy remains an issue for member states, with around 180 million people having insufficient or no access to electricity by 2022. There are significant disparities between member states and between urban and rural areas within each country. Electricity production remains insufficient, with a low penetration of renewable energy in mix. Transmission and distribution suffer from high commercial and technical losses, of the order of 21.5%, which are incompatible with the new production capacity needed to meet the growing demand from rapidly expanding urban areas.

ECOWAS Vision 2050 addresses these challenges as an integral part of achieving pillar 3 which is dedicated to « Infrastructure development and Interconnectivity ». The Vision document highlights the need to intensify the infrastructure development and interconnectivity to ensure availability and affordability of energy for the population.

To improve people's access to electricity, ECOWAS is working to establish a regional electricity market through the development of power generation and transmission infrastructure, and the intensification of its electricity access initiatives. With the financial support of the World Bank, ECOWAS has thus initiated the Regional Electricity Access Programme (REAP), which must normally be implemented in the form of a series of projects to gradually cover 11 countries, including 9 ECOWAS countries.

Phase 1 of the programme, entitled ECOWAS Regional Electricity Access Project (ECOWAS-REAP), covers The Gambia, Guinea Bissau and Mali. With a funding of 225 million USD, The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase access to electricity in the ECOWAS region through the strengthening and extension of electricity distribution infrastructure (MV and LV) and the connection of households in West African countries. The implementation covers the period 2019-2025. The target is to allow 2.04 million people to benefit from electricity service by 2025. Components of the project are the following: (i) construction of the electricity distribution networks, (ii) assistance of a owner engineer for the supervision of the works and (iii) project management and implementation coordination by local units (PIU) in the beneficiary countries and a regional coordination unit (RCU) in ECOWAS Directorate of Energy and Mines.

The regional coordination of the project is ensured by ECOWAS through a Regional Coordination Unit (RCU), and Project Implementation Units (PIUs) are established in each of the countries concerned.

    1. Major challenges during the implementation of the project
  • Emergence of Covid-19

The project financing agreements were signed in February 2019, and the preparation period for its implementation coincided with the emergence of Covid-19.

The outbreak of COVID-19 in early 2020 had widespread and unprecedented effects on the implementation of development projects worldwide, including World Bank–financed regional energy and infrastructure operations.

For multi-country projects, the pandemic created simultaneous disruptions across all participating countries, affecting implementation schedules, financial performance, and institutional capacity.

  • Institutional instability

The project was significantly affected by the change of political order that occurred in Mali in 2021 and subsequently in Guinea-Bissau in 2025. 

These political developments led to the temporary suspension of disbursements and activities by the World Bank, in accordance with its operational procedures regarding governance and eligibility of member states. 

This suspension, which extended over a prolonged period, resulted in: 

• a significant slowdown in the implementation of activities; 

• delays in the execution of ongoing contracts; 

• the postponement of certain supervision and technical assistance missions; 

• a negative impact on the project's performance indicators. 

The gradual resumption of activities required extensive technical and institutional exchanges in order to restore the required operational and fiduciary conditions.

  • Project Extension:

Taking into account the delays recorded in the implementation of activities, the three beneficiary countries (Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Mali) and the RCU submitted in 2025 official requests for project extensions. Following the review of these requests, the World Bank issued a favorable opinion, granting an extension of the project closing date until December 31, 2026. This extension will allow the completion of infrastructure works in the 3 countries and ensure the continuity of the regional coordination activities, in support to the PIUs.

• Additional funding

Gambia has negotiated additional funding to increase the number of beneficiary localities, going from 292 to 395, to further contribute to the increase of the electrification rate in the Country. The country target to reach universal access by 2026.

    1. Project Components 

The project comprises three components: (a) Design, supply, and installation of electricity distribution infrastructure (MV and LV) to maximize new connections; (b) Supervision of the construction and technical advisory services under Component 1 of the Project; and (c) Project coordination and technical assistance.

Component 1: Design, supply, and installation (DSI) of electricity distribution infrastructure (estimated cost: US$192 million equivalent, of which IDA US$192 million).

This component specifically supports (a) the detailed design, supply, and installation of distribution networks through the construction of approximately 3,900 km of 33 kilovolt (kV) MV lines, approximately 1,200 33KV/400 volt(V) distribution transformers, and approximately 3,700 km of 400 V LV lines to expand grid coverage and maximize the number of new connections; and (b) the supply and installation of last mile connection equipment, including service drops, smart meters for large consumers, prepaid meters, and ready boards for LV customers in each country and street lighting, all through the financing of non-consulting services, equipment and consulting services.

Component 2: Supervision of the construction and technical advisory services under Part 1 of

the Project (estimated cost: US$6 million equivalent, of which IDA US$6 million).

This component must finance the costs associated with the recruitment of an Owner’s Engineer who will be recruited on a competitive basis under the project to supervise the work carried out under Component 1. The Owner’s Engineer will also monitor compliance with safeguard instruments (environmental and social) related to construction. The responsibility of the Owner’s Engineer will comprise review of design, technical specifications, and bidding documents; supervision of procurement and construction; contract management; and supervision of implementation of an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) and Resettlement Action Plan (RAP). The Owner’s Engineer will assist each Project Implementation Unit (PIU) and the RCU during bid clarification, evaluation, and contract negotiation with the selected/awarded bidders/contractors.

Component 3: Project coordination and technical assistance (estimated cost: US$27 million

equivalent, of which IDA US$27 million).

In the spirit of strengthening national and regional capacities, this component will finance a combination of technical assistance and project management support to assist recipients in successfully implementing the project and preparing for future phases under the program. Specifically, this component will finance the strengthening of recipient implementation teams responsible for project implementation, expected project costs associated with the management of safeguards excluding the resettlement costs, and technical advisory services pertaining to preparation studies—such as least-cost electricity access development plans—for future projects in the region. The component will include two subcomponents.

  1. Rationale and Objectives of the End of Project Evaluation

The Project Financing Agreement was signed in regional by the ECOWAS’s Commission President on 19th, February 2019, and entered into force in the year 2021 at different date in each of beneficial country according to their context. Five years after the start of project implementation, the Regional Coordination Unit want to l undertake a comprehensive final evaluation to assess the overall performance of the project across all beneficiary countries. The evaluation will determine the extent to which the Project Development Objective was achieved, assess relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability, identify implementation challenges and lessons learned, and formulate strategic recommendations to guide the future of regional energy cooperation and subsequent operations. This report also will serve as the

    1. General objective 

The overall objective of this ECOWAS-REAP end of project evaluation is to assess the performance and results of the project at completion, determine the extent to which the Project Development Objective has been achieved, evaluate the relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability of project interventions, and provide evidence-based lessons and recommendations to inform future regional energy sector operations and policy decisions.

    1. Specific Objectives

The specific objectives of this final evaluation of the project are to:

  • Assess the Achievement of the Project Development Objective (PDO);
  • Evaluate the Relevance of the Project Design;
  • Assess the Effectiveness of Project Implementation;
  • Evaluate the Efficiency of Resource Utilization;
  • Assess the Impact of the Project;
  • Assess the Sustainability of Project Outcomes;
  • Examine the Effectiveness of Regional Coordination Mechanisms;
  • Review Environmental and Social Performance;
  • Analyze the Impact of External Factors and Risks;
  • Identify Lessons Learned and Best Practices;
  • Provide Strategic and Operational Recommendations;
  1. Expected Results

The end of project evaluation is expected to produce a comprehensive and independent assessment of the project’s performance, determine the extent of achievement of the Project Development Objective, identify lessons learned and good practices, and provide actionable recommendations to inform future operations and strategic decision-making at both national and regional levels.

  1. Duties and Mandate of the Consultant

The Consultant shall be responsible for conducting an independent and comprehensive final evaluation of the project, assessing its overall performance and achievement of development objectives, and preparing a high-quality Final Evaluation Report. The Consultant shall ensure methodological rigor, objectivity, and evidence-based analysis, and shall formulate actionable recommendations to inform future operations and regional energy programming.

The Consultant will perform the following tasks:

  • Conduct an independent assessment of project performance at completion;
  • Evaluate the achievement of the Project Development Objective (PDO) and results framework indicators;
  • Assess relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, and sustainability;
  • Identify implementation challenges, lessons learned, and good practices;
  • Provide practical and strategic recommendations for future programming.

The Consultant shall ensure impartiality, objectivity, and methodological rigor throughout the assignment.

Some Specific Duties and Responsibilities are requested in each phase as followed:

  1. Inception Phase

The Consultant at this phase shall:

  1. Review all relevant project documentation;
  2. Develop and submit an Inception Report.

Data Collection and Field Work Phase

The Consultant shall:

  1. Conduct consultations and interviews with all relevant stakeholders of the project;
  2. Undertake field visits to selected project sites in beneficiary countries;
  3. Collect and analyze quantitative and qualitative data to verify from countries reports;
  4. Validate findings through triangulation of multiple data sources

Analysis and Evaluation Phase

The Consultant shall:

  1. Assess project performance using recognized evaluation criteria (relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, sustainability);
  2. Evaluate financial, economic, institutional, environmental, and social performance ;
  3. Analyze the role and effectiveness of regional coordination mechanisms;
  4. Examine the impact of external factors (e.g., pandemics, political instability, force majeure events):
  5. Identify deviations from original design and analyze their implications.Reporting Phase

The Consultant shall prepare and submit:

  • Inception Report
  • Draft Final Evaluation Report (Interim Report)
  • Final Evaluation Report incorporating comments from stakeholders

The report shall be evidence-based, clearly structured, supported by data and based on the structure indicated at the annexe of the TOR.

The interim and the Final Report will be produced in three (03) hard copies and one (01) soft copy on electronic media (USB key) to be submitted to the Project Management Team.

NB: The reports must be produced in English and in French versions.

  1. Coordination and Communication

The Consultant shall:

  1. Work closely with the Regional Coordination Unit;
  2. Provide regular updates on progress;
  3. Present preliminary findings in a validation workshop (if required);
  4. Incorporate stakeholder feedback appropriately while preserving independence of conclusions
  1. Evaluation Methodology

The evaluation will adopt a mixed-methods approach combining desk review, key informant interviews, field visits, focus group discussions, and quantitative data analysis. Findings will be triangulated to ensure validity and reliability. The evaluation will assess performance against the Results Framework and internationally recognized evaluation criteria, and will include stakeholder validation prior to finalization of the report. 

  1. General aspect of the evaluation

The final evaluation will adopt a mixed-methods, participatory, and evidence-based approach, combining qualitative and quantitative data collection techniques to ensure accuracy, reliability, and objectivity of findings. The methodology will be aligned with internationally recognized evaluation standards and the requirements of World Bank. The evaluation will be structured around the following criteria:

  • Relevance
  • Effectiveness
  • Efficiency
  • Impact
  • Sustainability

For regional projects, particular attention will be given to cross-country comparison and the effectiveness of regional coordination mechanisms. All the details on the methodology is mentioned in the appendix attached this ToR.

  1. Other aspects the Evaluation Methodology
  •  Process and Reporting

The consultant will thoroughly familiarize himself/herself with the project documentation including the Financing Agreements, Grant Process and Agreements, Project Appraisal Document, Project Operation Manual, Environmental Safeguard documents, as well as key implementation documents such as annual work plans, progress reports, etc.

It is intended that all logistical arrangements will be made in consultation with REAP RCU and the PIU.

Key stakeholders will be consulted as part of the planning phase and clarify the commitments, responsibilities and expectations of Beneficiaries, World Bank, key stakeholders, appropriate Counterparts and the Individual Evaluator.

The Consultant is expected to consult relevant stakeholder throughout the assignment as one of the key inputs in carrying out the assignment. RCU of REAP, PIUs REAP, ECOWAS, World Bank, project consultants, representative of Ministry of Energy or Electrification Agencies will be consulted at all stages of the process.

  • Kick off meeting

The Consultant will prepare a Minutes of Meeting (MoM) following the kickoff meeting that will outline the methodology / approach to report preparation. This is to be done in consultation with the PIUs and RCU as well as the World Bank Team. The MoM of the kickoff meeting will include a schedule meeting with stakeholders.

  • Data Collection

Available data will be provided to the Consultant by the RUC and PIU. Additional qualitative and quantitative data / information should be collected in the field through a physical mission or by virtual video conference including consultations with a wide range of stakeholders. The consultant will be ensuring the quality of data (validity, reliability, consistency, and accuracy) throughout the final report.

  1. Duration

The total man-day of the assignment is estimated to 45 working days extended in 3 months. The mission is expected to Start on 1st September 2026 and an interim report will be submitted no later than December 1st, 2026. The final version with the invoice must submit no later than December 31st, 2026. 

  1. Qualification requirements

The Consultant shall possess a mix of evaluation skills and thematic knowledge. He/her must be a project and/or program evaluator specialist with significant experience. The Evaluator must have the following qualification/knowledge/expertise:

Minimum qualifications as an Independent Evaluator:

    1. A Master’s degree or equivalent in Energy, Economic, Statistics, Finances, Project management, Monitoring and Evaluation or Social Science, or other closely related fields;
    2. A minimum of 10 years’ experience in management and evaluation of development projects;
    3. Experience in designing evaluation tools that fit the need of the exercise,
    4. Must have conducted at least two similar missions;
    5. Experience and knowledge of Energy sector in West Africa will be advantage;
    6. Experience in evaluations of the World Bank and/or Development Banks programs and projects;
    7. Ability to write and speak fluently in English and in French.
  2. A Candidate will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (seventh Edition September 2025).
  3. The application documents should be composed of: Update CV, cover letter and supporting documents scanned in one pdf file.
  4. Further information and the Terms of reference  can be obtained only by email at the following email address: ecowas-reap@ecowas.int; with copy to banwone@ecowas.int, lkouassi@ecowas.int ; gouoba@ecowas.int and akoumoin@ecowas.int.
  5. Expressions of interest must be delivered latest by 21st,May 2026 at 5:00 pm GMT at ecowas-reap@ecowas.int; copying banwone@ecowas.int, lkouassi@ecowas.int ; gouoba@ecowas.int and akoumoin@ecowas.int.

NB:   Only the candidate ranked first after evaluation will be contacted for the rest of the procedure.

AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

Numéro de référence selon le PPM : BI-PACEJ-538579-CS-INDV

Services de Consultant : Consultant individuel (H/F), Assistant en suivi-évaluation pour les Projets Education

N° du don : IDA 8580

N° d’identification du Projet : P164416

Date de publication : 16/04/2026

Conscient de l'importance cruciale d'investir dans le capital humain pour garantir la stabilité nationale et impulser un développement durable, le Gouvernement du Burundi a désigné l'Education et la Santé comme secteurs prioritaires. À travers le Plan National de Développement 2018-2027 et la Vision de pays émergent 2040 et pays développé 2060 récemment adoptée, le Burundi s'engage à assurer un accès universel aux services de santé de base, à une éducation inclusive et de qualité pour tous, ainsi qu’au développement des compétences pour la diversification des emplois formels et la promotion de l’entreprenariat. Ces objectifs stratégiques visent à renforcer le capital humain à tous les niveaux de la société, réduisant ainsi les inégalités socio-économiques et stimulant une croissance pérenne.  Avec environ 41,5 % de la population âgée de 0 à 15 ans en 2022, les enfants du pays constituent sa richesse la plus abondante et détiennent la clé de la stabilité à long terme.

Par ailleurs, le Burundi abrite une importante population de réfugiés (86 300 en mars 2024 dont 39% âgés de 5 à 17 ans). En juin 2023, le Pays a mis à jour sa stratégie 2019 de soutien aux communautés d'accueil et aux réfugiés. Il s'engage à approfondir l'intégration des réfugiés et des rapatriés dans les systèmes nationaux et à leur intégration sociale, par, notamment l'harmonisation des systèmes d'éducation et de santé dans les zones de développement intégré. En matière d’éducation, le Pays élabore actuellement une stratégie pour l'inclusion des réfugiés et l'amélioration de l'accès des rapatriés au système éducatif burundais.

Les deux projets éducation en cours d’exécution sont :

procnotices.notice_text:
Jubbaland State of Somalia

Ministry of Interior, Federalism and Reconciliation

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

Individual Selection of Consultant

Country: Federal Government of Somalia

Project ID No. P508408

Name of the Project: Bulsho Project - Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience

Consulting Service: Bulsho Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist.

Individual/Firm: Individual

Ref No: SO-MOIFAR-545001-CS-INDV

Duty Station: Kismayo, Jubaland Somalia (with potential travel to the target Districts and Cities of Bulsho Project)

 

Deadline: 2nd May, 2026

 

BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT

 

The Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience (P508408) is under the lead of the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation – MoIFAR of the Federal Government of Somalia and responsible for the national program called Bulsho, the Somali word for society. The Bulsho Program puts citizens and communities at the center of the government’s action.  The Bulsho Program is a Somali government-led initiative designed to strengthen community and local institutions, fostering social cohesion, inclusion, and resilience. As Somalia continues its recovery from two decades of civil war, the program places a strong emphasis on enhancing service delivery, rebuilding the social contract, and promoting community-centered governance. This uniquely Somali-owned and -driven initiative underscores government ownership and leadership at federal, member state, and district levels, ensuring institutional sustainability and the realization of key policy outcomes.

The Ministry of Interior, Federalism and Reconciliation of Jubaland State of Somalia have established Project Implementation Units - PIUs, headed a State Project Managers, which have the responsibility for the activities that take place in Jubaland State.

The PIUs are responsible for managing project activities at state-level and to liaise with districts. Specifically, the PIUs are responsible for: (i) Verifying eligibility of districts, appraising districts’ request to participate – this includes allocation of Bulsho packages and conducting lottery for each package and verifying the fulfilment of district commitments. (ii) Preparing state-level procurement plans. (iii) Preparing annual project work plans and budgets for state-level activities. (iv) Carrying out procurement for state-level activities. (v) Managing the contract with the logistic firm. (vi) Delivering capacity building activities and providing quality assurance and technical backstopping to districts - this includes trainings of district officials and staff. as well as community entities that play a role in the project. (vii) Preparing requisitions for funds to be transferred to districts, as per the project workplan, and in accordance with the grant agreement/sub-agreements and this POM and its annexes. (viii) Preparing quarterly narrative and financial reports for project activities taking place in their states. (ix) Verifying technical and E&S appraisal of local investments (Component 3) as well as other E&S actions as per the Environment and Social Management Plan. (x) Verifying the soundness of sustainability plans for the local investment prepared by the districts, including Operations & Maintenance (O&M) plans and the Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) for the management of local infrastructures; and (xi) Preparing security management plans and applying security protocols in partnership with the security firm.

The Ministry of Interior, Federalism and Reconciliation of Jubaland State of Somalia is seeking to use a portion of the Bulsho Project to finance the recruitment of a Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist to support the Jubaland Project Implementation Unit - PIU.

Responsibilities: For the Bulsho Project activities, the Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist at the PIU will be responsible for implementing Bulsho’s social development and gender inclusion agenda at the state and district levels. The Specialist will ensure that Local Social Contract Platforms - LSCPs, Citizens’ Charters, and community planning processes are inclusive, participatory and responsive to the needs of women, youth, minorities, IDPs and other marginalized groups.

The Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist at the PIU will be responsible for implementing Bulsho’s social development and gender inclusion agenda at the state and district levels. The Specialist will ensure that Local Social Contract Platforms - LSCPs, Citizens’ Charters, and community planning processes are inclusive, participatory and responsive to the needs of women, youth, minorities, IDPs and other marginalized groups. The Specialist will support districts and communities in preparing and applying social risk management measures, developing grievance redress mechanisms, and implementing gender-sensitive approaches in community-driven investments.  The role combines both social safeguarding and gender responsibilities, providing practical support and monitoring to ensure that Bulsho-funded investments contribute to equitable, inclusive and sustainable local development.

The PIU Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist will work closely with the PCU Social Safeguarding Specialist and the PIU the Local Government and Community Development Specialist

Selection Criteria: The selection shall be based on qualification, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include:

1. Educational Background

  • University degree in sociology, social development, human rights, gender studies, anthropology, economics, public administration, social works, development studies. A master’s degree in the above fields is an advantage.

 2. Professional Experience

  • Minimum of 7 years of professional experience in social safeguards or social development, inclusion, or gender-focused programs. (Note: pre-university graduation experiences will be not counted)
  • A minimum of five (5) years of professional experience in social development, community engagement, social risk management, or related fields, with at least two (2) years in fragile, conflict-affected, and/or FCV contexts.
  • Familiarity with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or equivalent international social safeguards frameworks, or demonstrated willingness and ability to learn
  • Demonstrated experience in conducting social screening, preparing social safeguard inputs to ESMPs, and monitoring social risk mitigation measures.
  • Proven track record in facilitating participatory planning and ensuring inclusion of women, youth, minorities, IDPs, and marginalized groups.
  • Proven track record in capacity building of local governments, community institutions, and civil society actors. Note: Experience limited to policy development, advisory roles, or research without direct involvement in implementation of community-level processes will not be considered sufficient.

 3. Skills and competencies

  • Strong facilitation and community engagement skills, with the ability to promote gender equality and inclusion in practice.
  • Practical experience in establishing and managing grievance redress mechanisms (GRM).
  • Ability to train and mentor local government officials and community institutions.
  • Strong interpersonal, facilitation, and communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with community members, local authorities, and development partners.

 4. Knowledge

  • Good understanding of the World Bank ESF, ESCP, and social safeguard instruments.
  • Familiarity with Somalia’s social dynamics, governance structures, and challenges to inclusion, especially in the state and at local level.
  • Awareness of gender and social development issues in fragile and conflict-affected contexts.
  • Ability and willingness to undertake regular field travel to project target districts within the FMS, subject to security clearance.

 5. Language skills/requirement.

  • Excellent command of Somali language, e.g., reading, writing and presenting is essential
  • Excellent command of English language, e.g., reading, writing and presenting is essential.

REPORTING

The Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist will report to the Jubaland Bulsho PIU Project Manager.

TIMING Duration of Assignment:

The Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist shall be contracted for up to 12 months and renewable upon satisfactory performance.

The Ministry of Interior, Federalism and Reconciliation of Jubaland State of Somalia now invites eligible individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide the following (i) Curriculum Vitae (CV) with 3 reference persons; (ii) copies of certificates of academic qualifications; and (iii) cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. (Female candidates who meet the required qualifications are strongly encouraged to apply for the position of Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist)

Interested candidates should submit their applications, including a detailed updated CV and cover letter, outlining their experience and qualifications in relation to the role marked with the subject title of the position by the following email address: adminfinance-mo@jubalandstate.so and copy to sharlaawe17@gmail.com and Abdirahman.ahmed@moifar.gov.so latest by 2nd May, 2026 at 04:00 PM Mogadishu time.

 

Attention:

Bulsho PIU Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist

Ministry of Interior, Federalism and Reconciliation

Jubaland State of Somalia

Kismayo, Jubaland, Somalia

Livestock Technical Advisor – Jubaland State

Individual

1. BACKGROUND

The Somalia Food Systems Resilience Program (FSRP) is part of a regional initiative by the World Bank to provide a comprehensive framework to intervene at both the national and regional levels. This Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA) aims to tackle the underlying structural challenges of food insecurity and reduce beneficiaries' vulnerability to unpredictable climate, crisis, and conflict events. It seeks to achieve this by strengthening Somalia's agri-livestock research institutions, extension services, and community institutions to support climate-smart agriculture and livestock practices, improving water availability, rangeland management, animal health services, and strengthening access to markets and value addition.

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase preparedness against food insecurity and improve the resilience of food systems in targeted project areas of Somalia.

The Jubaland State of Somalia is implementing the project through the Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation in close consultation and collaboration with the Ministry of Livestock, Rangeland and Forestry (MoLFR). The Project Coordination Unit (PIU) supports coordination, Facilitation, and monitoring of project activities.

 

2. Scope of Work and Responsibilities

The Livestock Technical Advisor will be a full-time contracted individual assigned to the Project Coordination Unit (PCU) within the Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation, Jubaland State. The advisor will provide technical support to strengthen livestock production systems, focusing on animal nutrition, fodder development, rangeland management, and animal health, while working closely with the Ministry of Livestock, Rangeland and Forestry.

The Livestock Technical Advisor will be responsible for the following duties:

  • Provide technical advice to the Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation and work closely with the Ministry of Livestock, Rangeland and Forestry on livestock sector development, particularly fodder production, storage, and marketing strategies
  • Support implementation of livestock-related project activities, including feed resource development, animal nutrition, and feed safety
  • Develop strategies and guidelines for improving livestock feeding systems and utilization of feed resources
  • Support emergency and supplementary feeding interventions in coordination with relevant ministries
  • Conduct community consultations on livestock needs and feed systems
  • Assist in development of guidelines for mobile veterinary clinics
  • Support planning and implementation of animal health and productivity programs in coordination with MoLFR
  • Coordinate training programs for extension staff, community animal health workers, and stakeholders
  • Participate in technical meetings, prepare reports, and contribute to knowledge products
  • Facilitate coordination among Ministries (MoAI, MoLFR), NGOs, and producer organizations
  • Support procurement processes related to livestock activities.
  • Document best practices, lessons learned, and success stories.
  • Prepare regular progress reports aligned with project results framework.

3. Selection Criteria

The selection shall be based on qualifications, experience, and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications and competencies include:

  • A Bachelor Degree or Master in Veterinary Medicine, Animal Production, Animal Science, or a related field
  • Minimum of 6 years of experience in livestock production, animal health, or fodder systems, preferably in Somalia
  • Experience working with pastoral and agro-pastoral communities
  • Experience in fodder production, feed systems, and rangeland management
  • Experience in training delivery, extension services, and policy support
  • Practical experience in project implementation, monitoring and evaluation, and reporting
  • Strong analytical and technical report writing skills
  • Excellent communication skills in Somali and English
  • Strong interpersonal and coordination skills
  • Good computer skills including Microsoft Office tools

4. REPORTING

The Livestock Technical Advisor will report to the State Project Coordinator, Accountable to DG Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation as Project Technical Lead, Jubaland State, and will work in close coordination with the Ministry of Livestock, Rangeland and Forestry.

5. Duration of Assignment

The assignment shall be for a period of 12 months, with the possibility of extension based on satisfactory performance.

6. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. 

Interested applicants may obtain further information including a detailed Terms of Reference from the Ministry in person or by e-mail to the address given below during office hours from 9.00 a.m.– 4.00 p.m. Saturday to Thursday.

procnotices.notice_text:
Requests for Quotations

The Project Management Unit, Board of Revenue, Govt. of Punjab has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Punjab Urban Land Systems Enhancement (PULSE) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the following contract:

Hiring of Firm for

Data Entry and Scanning of Newly Established Housing Societies PHATA and Development Authorities

The quotations are invited from well reputed registered firms having NTN and GST Registration for the provision of above-mentioned services. The complete quotation along with all required documents must reach this office by 29.04.2026 till 11:00 AM. Any quotation received after the scheduled time shall not be entertained and would be returned unopened.

Requests for Quotations (RFQ) can be obtained from this office during office working hours or downloaded from the PULSE website https://pulse.gop.pk. Procurement will be conducted through the Requests for Quotations method, as specified in the World Bank “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers –November-2020” and is open to all eligible suppliers as defined in the Procurement Regulations. 

Service Providers are requested to give their best and final prices as negotiations are not allowed. Interested parties may obtain further information from below mentioned address.

Procurement Specialist

Punjab Urban Land Systems Enhancement (PULSE)

Project Management Unit, Board of Revenue

Government of the Punjab, Pakistan

158-A Abu Bakar Block, New Garden Town, Lahore.

Ph: 042-37882061-63

Email: pspmupulse@punjab-zameen.gov.pk

Web: https://pulse.gop.pk

procnotices.project_name: Support for Resilient Livelihoods in the South of Madagascar - MIONJO Project
procnotices.bid_description: Spécialiste Régional en environnement
procnotices.contact_organization: MIONJO
procnotices.notice_text:
APPEL A CANDIDATURES

UN(E) (01) SPECIALISTE REGIONAL EN ENVIRONNEMENT BASE A ANDROY

 AMI N° : 544575/26/AMI/UNGP/MIONJO

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet soutien aux moyens de subsistance résilients dans le Sud de Madagascar « MIONJO » et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce fonds à des services de consultant.
  2. Les services de consultant (« les Services ») consistent à fournir un appui technique et opérationnel au niveau des sites d’intervention du Projet dans la mise en œuvre des activités de mise en place des infrastructures vertes et Paysages Résilients afin de lutter contre la désertification et promouvoir la résilience climatique. Ils consistent également à contribuer à l’amélioration des capacités des acteurs en matière de résilience climatique et de travailler en étroite collaboration avec les autres volets pour une meilleure coordination sectorielle.
  3. Les Termes de Référence (TDR) pour la mission sont disponibles sur le site internet suivant : https://mionjo.mg ou sur demande à adresser à procurement@mionjo.mg .
  4. L'Unité Nationale de Gestion du Projet (UNGP) MIONJO invite dès à présent les consultants admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services. Les critères de sélection sont les suivants :

Qualifications et expériences :

  • Titulaire d’au moins un Bac+4 en Foresterie ou en Sciences Naturelles, ou en Environnement ;
  • Avoir au moins 5 ans d’expériences professionnelles en foresterie et développement durable ;
  • Avoir au moins 3 ans d’expériences en sylviculture ;
  • Avoir au moins 3 expériences professionnelles dans le cadre de projet sur le changement climatique
  • Bonne connaissance des différents outils de planification et de gestion de projet ;
  • Langues :
    • Pratique courante du malgache et du français (écrit et oral) ;
    • Atouts :
      • Expériences pratique dans des activités de fixation des dunes ;
      • Connaissance en SIG et télédétection
      • Pratique des dialectes locaux des zones d’intervention du Projet ;
      • Pratique courante de l’anglais (écrit et oral).

Qualités et aptitudes :

  • Rigueur et intégrité ;
  • Capacités d’analyse, de synthèse, de rédaction et de communication ;
  • Proactivité ;
  • Aptitude à travailler sous pression et à gérer des deadlines ;
  • Disponibilité à descendre sur terrain, notamment dans des zones rurales reculées

Les candidats qualifiés seront convoqués à un entretien.

  1. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI » de la Banque mondiale, septième édition Septembre 2025 (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés »), qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts. En outre, veuillez-vous reporter aux informations spécifiques suivantes sur les conflits d’intérêts liés à cette mission : « Le Consultant qui a une relation professionnelle ou familiale étroite avec tout cadre de l’Emprunteur, de l’organisme d’exécution du projet, d’un bénéficiaire d’une fraction du financement de la Banque ou de toute autre partie représentant l’Emprunteur ou agissant en son nom qui participe directement ou indirectement à tout segment : (i) de la préparation des Termes de référence de la mission ; (ii) du processus de sélection pour le contrat ; ou (iii) de la supervision du contrat, ne peut être attributaire d’un contrat, sauf si le conflit résultant de ladite relation a été réglé d’une manière que la Banque juge satisfaisante tout au long du processus de sélection et de l’exécution du contrat ».
  2. Le Consultant sera sélectionné conformément aux dispositions décrites dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.
  3. Des informations supplémentaires peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau de 09h00 à 17h00 heures locales.
  4. Les manifestations d’intérêt contenant (i) une lettre de motivation avec prétention salariale, et la disponibilité rédigée en français, (ii) un CV détaillé mise à jour (modèle annexé aux TdRs), références avec coordonnées (au moins deux), coordonnées téléphoniques pour contact rapide et (iii) les copies des diplômes et les Certificats prouvant les expériences professionnelles, seront adressées au Coordonnateur du Projet MIONJO et envoyées à l’adresse ci-dessous (en personne, par la poste, ou par courriel) au plus tard le 04 mai  2026.

Adresse : Lot II A 105 G Nanisana Iadiambola, Antananarivo 101

Courriel : procurement@mionjo.mg  et rpm@mionjo.mg

Et portant la mention « AMI N° 544575/26/AMI/UNGP/MIONJO – SPECIALISTE REGIONAL EN ENVIRONNEMENT.

Antananarivo le, 16 avril 2026

Mozambique Digital Acceleration Project (MDAP)

The Government of Mozambique has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Digital Acceleration Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Implement capacity‑building activities in ICT for the Ministry of Education.

 

The objective of this assignment is to equip professionals in the Education sector with essential digital skills for the efficient delivery of services. This enhancement aims to accelerate digital transformation and strengthen the modernization of the sector.

In carrying out the activities, the firm must work closely with the MEC, represented by the Human Resources Department (HR Dept) and the IT Dept. These units will coordinate and supervise the entire process and provide the necessary support for implementing the activities. The MEC, in turn, must report the status to the PIU of the MDAP. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria are: i) The firm must be experienced in providing ICT professional training and capacity-building services at least 5 years; ii) Proven track record in managing and implementing large-scale ICT training programs at a national or regional level; iii) Documented evidence of successfully delivering training in at least one of the following specialized areas: Productivity Tools: Office suites (Excel, Word, Power Point, etc.); Advanced ICT Skills: Systems Administration, Help Desk, and Computer/Network Hardware Maintenance; Software Engineering: proficiency in modern programming languages such as Java, Python, etc. Experience in Digital Pedagogy or training educators for e-learning environments. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

procnotices.notice_text:
South West State

Ministry of Interior, Local Government & Reconciliation

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

 

Individual Selection of Consultant

Country: Federal Government of Somalia

Project ID No. P508408

Name of the Project: Bulsho Project - Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience

Consulting Service: Bulsho PIU Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning – MEAL Specialist.

Individual/Firm: Individual

Ref No: SO-MOIFAR-540748-CS-INDV

Duty Station: Baidoa, South West, Somalia (with potential travel to the target Districts and Cities of Bulsho Project)

Deadline: 2nd May, 2026

BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT

The Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience (P508408) is under the lead of the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation – MoIFAR of the Federal Government of Somalia and responsible for the national program called Bulsho, the Somali word for society. The Bulsho Program puts citizens and communities at the center of the government’s action.  The Bulsho Program is a Somali government-led initiative designed to strengthen community and local institutions, fostering social cohesion, inclusion, and resilience. As Somalia continues its recovery from two decades of civil war, the program places a strong emphasis on enhancing service delivery, rebuilding the social contract, and promoting community-centered governance. This uniquely Somali-owned and -driven initiative underscores government ownership and leadership at federal, member state, and district levels, ensuring institutional sustainability and the realization of key policy outcomes.

The Ministry of Interior, Local Government and Reconciliation of South West State of Somalia have established Project Implementation Units - PIUs, headed a State Project Managers, which have the responsibility for the activities that take place in South West State.

The PIUs are responsible for managing project activities at state-level and to liaise with districts. Specifically, the PIUs are responsible for: (i) Verifying eligibility of districts, appraising districts’ request to participate – this includes allocation of Bulsho packages and conducting lottery for each package and verifying the fulfilment of district commitments. (ii) Preparing state-level procurement plans. (iii) Preparing annual project work plans and budgets for state-level activities. (iv) Carrying out procurement for state-level activities. (v) Managing the contract with the logistic firm. (vi) Delivering capacity building activities and providing quality assurance and technical backstopping to districts - this includes trainings of district officials and staff. as well as community entities that play a role in the project. (vii) Preparing requisitions for funds to be transferred to districts, as per the project workplan, and in accordance with the grant agreement/sub-agreements and this POM and its annexes. (viii) Preparing quarterly narrative and financial reports for project activities taking place in their states. (ix) Verifying technical and E&S appraisal of local investments (Component 3) as well as other E&S actions as per the Environment and Social Management Plan. (x) Verifying the soundness of sustainability plans for the local investment prepared by the districts, including Operations & Maintenance (O&M) plans and the Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) for the management of local infrastructures; and (xi) Preparing security management plans and applying security protocols in partnership with the security firm.

The Ministry of Interior, Local Government and Reconciliation of South West State of Somalia is seeking to use a portion of the Bulsho Project to finance the recruitment of a Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning - MEAL Specialist to support the South West Project Implementation Unit - PIU.

Responsibilities: For the Bulsho Project activities, the main objective of the assignment is to ensure effective monitoring and evaluation of the Bulsho Project at the state and district levels, through the collection, verification, and reporting of MIS data; close collaboration with district staff; and coordination with the Knowledge Management and Research Firm on survey-based data collection, in line with the Project Operations Manual (POM), the project Results Framework (RF), the project Monitoring and Evaluation Plan (MEP), World Bank requirements.

The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning – MEAL Specialist will work in close coordination with, and provide support to, the PCU M&E Specialist, as well as collaborate with the PCU & PIUs Social Safeguarding, Environmental Specialist, the Local Government & Community Development Specialist, and also Third-Party Monitoring and Digital Innovation Firms to ensure that all M&E activities comply with the project’s Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), ethical research standards, and SEA/SH prevention measures.

Selection Criteria: The selection shall be based on qualification, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include:

1. Educational Background

  • University degree in Statistics, Data Science, Computer Technology/Science, Economics, Social Sciences, Public Administration, Political Science, Development Studies. Master’s degree in the above field is an asset.

 2. Professional Experience

  • Minimum of 7 years of professional experience in M&E for donor-funded projects in fragile/conflict-affected contexts, preferably in Somalia or the East Africa region. Note: pre-university graduation experiences will be not counted).
  • Experience in community-level data collection, site verification, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Strong skills in data entry, validation, and basic analysis using MIS platforms, statistical software and data tools (e.g., STATA, SPSS, Excel, KoBoToolbox).
  • Experience supporting survey operations and working with contracted research firms.
  • Excellent communication skills in Somali and English, with proven ability to write clear and concise reports.
  • Knowledge of World Bank M&E requirements and results frameworks is an advantage.

 3. Skills and competencies

  • Strong analytical and data interpretation skills.
  • Proficient in applying M&E frameworks and use M&E tools (e.g., logframes, indicators).
  • Skilled in both qualitative and quantitative research methods.
  • Experience with data collection, analysis, and visualization tools (e.g., Excel, SPSS, Power BI).

 4. Knowledge

  • In-depth understanding of M&E principles, RBM, and Theory of Change.
  • Familiarity with donor M&E requirements (e.g., World Bank, UN, USAID).
  • Knowledge of Somalia’s socio-political and institutional context.
  • Understanding of cross-cutting themes: gender, inclusion, conflict sensitivity.
  • Experience with statistical software (e.g., STATA, SPSS, R) and digital data collection tools (e.g., KoboToolbox, ODK).
  • Knowledge of adaptive management and using M&E for decision-making.

 5. Language skills/requirement.

  • Excellent command of Somali language, e.g., reading, writing and presenting is essential
  • Excellent command of English language, e.g., reading, writing and presenting is essential.

REPORTING

The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning - MEAL Specialist will report to the South West Bulsho PIU Project Manager.

TIMING Duration of Assignment:

The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning - MEAL Specialist shall be contracted for up to 12 months and renewable upon satisfactory performance.

The Ministry of Interior, Local Government and Reconciliation of South West State of Somalia now invites eligible individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide the following (i) Curriculum Vitae (CV) with 3 reference persons; (ii) copies of certificates of academic qualifications; and (iii) cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. 

Interested candidates should submit their applications, including a detailed updated CV and cover letter, outlining their experience and qualifications in relation to the role marked with the subject title of the position by the following email address:  hr@moilgr.sw.so and  Abdirahman.ahmed@moifar.gov.so latest by 2nd May, 2026 at 04:00 PM Mogadishu time.

 

Attention:

Bulsho PIU Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning - MEAL Specialist

Ministry of Interior, Local Government and Reconciliation

South West State of Somalia

Baidoa, South West, Somalia

AVIS D’APPEL D’OFFRES NATIONAL  N°012/2026 

(Procédure à enveloppe unique)

Pays : République du Tchad

Nom du Projet : Projet pour l’Autonomisation des Femmes et le Dividende Démographique en Afrique Sub-Saharienne Plus (SWEDD+).

Numéro du Don : IDA-E2400.

Reference PPM N° TD-SWEDD–TD-531551-GO-RFB   

Intitulé du Marché : Appel d’Offres National N°012/ MFBEPCI/SE/SG/SWEDD+/PM/2026,

Relatif à l’acquisition des kits d’accouchement pour renforcer les maternités dans la zone d’intervention  du projet et l’hôpital de la mère et enfants .

 

Sous-composante 2.3 « Améliorer la disponibilité des agents de santé de la reproduction dans les zones rurales, en renforçant les Sagefemmes rurales et les autres personnels impliqués dans les services de prévention de RMNCAHN ».          

 

La République du Tchad a reçu un Don de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA) pour financer les activités du Projet pour l’Autonomisation des Femmes et le Dividende Démographique en Afrique Sub-Saharienne Plus (SWEDD+), et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce Don pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché relatif à l’acquisition des kits d’accouchement pour renforcer les maternités dans la zone d’intervention  du projet et l’hôpital de la mère et enfants sous-composante 2.3 « Améliorer la disponibilité des agents de santé de la reproduction dans les zones rurales, en renforçant les Sagefemmes rurales et les autres personnels impliqués dans les services de prévention de RMNCAHN ».

Le ministère des Finances, du Budget, de l’Economie et du Plan à travers le Projet pour l’Autonomisation des Femmes et le Dividende Démographique en Afrique Sub-Saharienne Plus (SWEDD+) sollicite des offres de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour fournir les équipements objet de cet appel d’offre.

La procédure sera conduite par mise en concurrence nationale en recourant à un Appel d’Offres National (AON) telle que définie dans le « Règlement applicable aux Emprunteurs – Passation des Marchés dans le cadre de Financement de Projets d’Investissement  Directives : « Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des services de Consultants et Services de Consultants de Juillet 2016, révisé en septembre         2017, août 2018 et Novembre 2020» de la Banque Mondiale (« le Règlement de passation des marchés »), et ouverte à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans les Règles de passation des marchés.

Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de : Unité de Gestion du Projet SWEDD+, sise au quartier Repos, Rue de 30m, dans le 4ème arrondissement à côté du Lycée de la Liberté. Tel : (+235) 22 53 10 56 Courriel : sweddtchad@gmail.com ; BP : 2268 N’Djaména – Tchad et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres à l’adresse e-mail mentionnée ci-dessus de 7 heures à 15 heures 30 minutes tous les jours et les vendredis de 7 heures à 12 heures 30 minutes, heure locale.

Le Dossier d’Appel d’offres en Français peut être acheté par tout Soumissionnaire intéressé en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse ci-dessous contre un paiement non remboursable de 100 000 FCFA. La méthode de paiement sera en espèces contre reçu. Pour les fournisseurs étrangers qui désirent avoir le dossier via DHL ou autres, le frais de transfert est à la charge du fournisseur. Le dossier d’appel d’offres sera adressé sous pli fermé.

Les offres devront être remises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le 19/05/2026 à 10 heures précises, heures locales. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires et des personnes présentes à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessus le 19/05/2026 à 10 heures 30 minutes, heure locale.

Les offres doivent être accompagnées d’une Garantie de soumission, pour un montant égal au moins à 2% du montant de l’offre.

Les adresses auxquelles il est fait référence ci-dessus sont : Unité de Gestion du Projet SWEDD+, sise au quartier Repos, Rue de 30m, dans le 4ème arrondissement à côté du Lycée de la Liberté. Tel : (+235) 22 53 10 56 Courriel : sweddtchad@gmail.com ; BP : 2268 N’Djaména–Tchad.

N’Djaména, le 16 avril 2026

Le  Coordonnateur National du Projet SWEDD+

 

YOUSSOUF AWARE NEISSA

JUBALAND STATE OF SOMALIA

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

Individual Selection of Consultant

Clarification Information

Item

Description

Country

Federal Government of Somalia

Project ID No.

P177816

Project Name

Somalia Food Systems Resilience Project – Phase 3 (S-FSRP III)

Consulting Service

Livestock Disease Specialist – Jubaland State

Individual/Firm

Individual Consultant (INDV)

Duty Station

Kismayo

Deadline

7th May 2026

 

1. BACKGROUND

The Somalia Food Systems Resilience Program (FSRP) is part of a regional initiative by the World Bank to provide a comprehensive framework to intervene at both the national and regional levels. This Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA) aims to tackle the underlying structural challenges of food insecurity and reduce beneficiaries' vulnerability to unpredictable climate, crisis, and conflict events. It seeks to achieve this by strengthening Somalia's agri-livestock research institutions, extension services, and community institutions to support climate-smart agriculture and livestock practices, improving water availability, rangeland management, animal health services, and strengthening access to markets and value addition.

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase preparedness against food insecurity and improve the resilience of food systems in targeted project areas of Somalia.

The Jubaland State of Somalia is implementing the project through the Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation in close collaboration with the Ministry of Livestock, Rangeland and Forestry. The Project Coordination Unit (PCU) supports coordination, Facilitating, and monitoring of project activities.

2. Scope of Work and Responsibilities

The Livestock Disease Specialist will be a full-time contracted individual assigned to the Project Coordination Unit (PCU) within the Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation, Jubaland State. The specialist will be responsible for developing and implementing strategies to mitigate livestock diseases and strengthen animal health systems, while working closely with the Ministry of Livestock, Rangeland and Forestry.

The Livestock Disease Specialist will be responsible for the following duties:

  • Conduct livestock health assessments and identify prevalent diseases
  • Develop disease prevention and control strategies tailored to local contexts
  • Collaborate closely with the Ministry of Livestock, Rangeland and Forestry, farmers, and veterinary services to improve disease management practices
  • Strengthen livestock disease surveillance and early warning systems
  • Train community members and stakeholders on livestock health management practices
  • Integrate local knowledge into disease surveillance systems
  • Monitor and evaluate effectiveness of disease control interventions
  • Support implementation of livestock health activities under the project in coordination with relevant ministries
  • Participate in coordination meetings and technical discussions with MoAI, MoLFR, and stakeholders
  • Prepare technical reports and documentation aligned with project objectives

3. Selection Criteria

The selection shall be based on qualifications, experience, and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications and competencies include:

  • A Master or Bachelor degree in Veterinary Medicine or a related field
  • 6 years or more Strong experience in livestock disease management and epidemiology
  • Experience in disease surveillance systems and livestock health programs
  • Familiarity with pastoral and agro-pastoral systems in Somalia
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Good communication skills in Somali and English
  • Experience working with communities and stakeholders
  • Strong coordination skills with government institutions
  • Commitment to sustainable livestock and resilience-building practices

4. REPORTING

The Livestock Disease Specialist will report to the State Project Coordinator, DG Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation as Lead Technical, Jubaland State, and will work in close coordination with the Ministry of Livestock, Rangeland and Forestry.

 

5. Duration of Assignment

The assignment shall be for a period of 12 months, with the possibility of extension based on satisfactory performance.

6. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. 

Interested applicants may obtain further information including a detailed Terms of Reference from the Ministry in person or by e-mail to the address given below during office hours from 9.00 a.m.– 4.00 p.m. Saturday to Thursday.

Deadline: Expressions of interest and CV must be delivered to the address below by hand, mail, courier or email on or before 07 May 2026 at 16:00 hours.

Puntland Government of Somalia

Bulsho Project - Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

Individual Selection of Consultant

Country: Federal Government of Somalia

Project ID No. P508408

Name of the Project: Bulsho Project - Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience

Consulting Service: Bulsho Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist.

Individual/Firm: Individual

Ref No: SO-MOIFAR-545002-CS-INDV

Duty Station: Garowe, Puntland Somalia (with potential travel to the target Districts and Cities of Bulsho Project)

Deadline: 2nd May, 2026

 

BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT

The Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience (P508408) is under the lead of the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation – MoIFAR of the Federal Government of Somalia and responsible for the national program called Bulsho, the Somali word for society. The Bulsho Program puts citizens and communities at the center of the government’s action.  The Bulsho Program is a Somali government-led initiative designed to strengthen community and local institutions, fostering social cohesion, inclusion, and resilience. As Somalia continues its recovery from two decades of civil war, the program places a strong emphasis on enhancing service delivery, rebuilding the social contract, and promoting community-centered governance. This uniquely Somali-owned and -driven initiative underscores government ownership and leadership at federal, member state, and district levels, ensuring institutional sustainability and the realization of key policy outcomes.

The Ministry of Interior, Federalism and Democratisation of Puntland State of Somalia have established Project Implementation Units - PIUs, headed a State Project Managers, which have the responsibility for the activities that take place in Puntland State.

The PIUs are responsible for managing project activities at state-level and to liaise with districts. Specifically, the PIUs are responsible for: (i) Verifying eligibility of districts, appraising districts’ request to participate – this includes allocation of Bulsho packages and conducting lottery for each package and verifying the fulfilment of district commitments. (ii) Preparing state-level procurement plans. (iii) Preparing annual project work plans and budgets for state-level activities. (iv) Carrying out procurement for state-level activities. (v) Managing the contract with the logistic firm. (vi) Delivering capacity building activities and providing quality assurance and technical backstopping to districts - this includes trainings of district officials and staff. as well as community entities that play a role in the project. (vii) Preparing requisitions for funds to be transferred to districts, as per the project workplan, and in accordance with the grant agreement/sub-agreements and this POM and its annexes. (viii) Preparing quarterly narrative and financial reports for project activities taking place in their states. (ix) Verifying technical and E&S appraisal of local investments (Component 3) as well as other E&S actions as per the Environment and Social Management Plan. (x) Verifying the soundness of sustainability plans for the local investment prepared by the districts, including Operations & Maintenance (O&M) plans and the Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) for the management of local infrastructures; and (xi) Preparing security management plans and applying security protocols in partnership with the security firm.

The Ministry of Interior, Federalism and Democratisation of Puntland State of Somalia is seeking to use a portion of the Bulsho Project to finance the recruitment of a Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist to support the Puntland Project Implementation Unit - PIU.

Responsibilities: For the Bulsho Project activities, the Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist at the PIU will be responsible for implementing Bulsho’s social development and gender inclusion agenda at the state and district levels. The Specialist will ensure that Local Social Contract Platforms - LSCPs, Citizens’ Charters, and community planning processes are inclusive, participatory and responsive to the needs of women, youth, minorities, IDPs and other marginalized groups.

The Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist at the PIU will be responsible for implementing Bulsho’s social development and gender inclusion agenda at the state and district levels. The Specialist will ensure that Local Social Contract Platforms - LSCPs, Citizens’ Charters, and community planning processes are inclusive, participatory and responsive to the needs of women, youth, minorities, IDPs and other marginalized groups. The Specialist will support districts and communities in preparing and applying social risk management measures, developing grievance redress mechanisms, and implementing gender-sensitive approaches in community-driven investments.  The role combines both social safeguarding and gender responsibilities, providing practical support and monitoring to ensure that Bulsho-funded investments contribute to equitable, inclusive and sustainable local development.

The PIU Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist will work closely with the PCU Social Safeguarding Specialist and the PIU the Local Government and Community Development Specialist

Selection Criteria: The selection shall be based on qualification, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include:

1. Educational Background

  • University degree in sociology, social development, human rights, gender studies, anthropology, economics, public administration, social works, development studies. A master’s degree in the above fields is an advantage.

 2. Professional Experience

  • Minimum of 7 years of professional experience in social safeguards or social development, inclusion, or gender-focused programs. (Note: pre-university graduation experiences will be not counted)
  • A minimum of five (5) years of professional experience in social development, community engagement, social risk management, or related fields, with at least two (2) years in fragile, conflict-affected, and/or FCV contexts.
  • Familiarity with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or equivalent international social safeguards frameworks, or demonstrated willingness and ability to learn
  • Demonstrated experience in conducting social screening, preparing social safeguard inputs to ESMPs, and monitoring social risk mitigation measures.
  • Proven track record in facilitating participatory planning and ensuring inclusion of women, youth, minorities, IDPs, and marginalized groups.
  • Proven track record in capacity building of local governments, community institutions, and civil society actors. Note: Experience limited to policy development, advisory roles, or research without direct involvement in implementation of community-level processes will not be considered sufficient.

 3. Skills and competencies

  • Strong facilitation and community engagement skills, with the ability to promote gender equality and inclusion in practice.
  • Practical experience in establishing and managing grievance redress mechanisms (GRM).
  • Ability to train and mentor local government officials and community institutions.
  • Strong interpersonal, facilitation, and communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with community members, local authorities, and development partners.

 4. Knowledge

  • Good understanding of the World Bank ESF, ESCP, and social safeguard instruments.
  • Familiarity with Somalia’s social dynamics, governance structures, and challenges to inclusion, especially in the state and at local level.
  • Awareness of gender and social development issues in fragile and conflict-affected contexts.
  • Ability and willingness to undertake regular field travel to project target districts within the FMS, subject to security clearance.

 5. Language skills/requirement.

  • Excellent command of Somali language, e.g., reading, writing and presenting is essential
  • Excellent command of English language, e.g., reading, writing and presenting is essential.

REPORTING

The Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist will report to the Puntland Bulsho PIU Project Manager.

TIMING Duration of Assignment:

The Social Safeguarding and Gender Specialist shall be contracted for up to 12 months and renewable upon satisfactory performance.
